name: Bud Green
lede: Bud green is a fresh leaf green named for the unfolding buds of spring.

sections.title: A yellowish green
sections.body:
Paterson defines bud green as a yellowish-green [1]. His indexes place it with the greens, among avocado, bottle green and chartreuse [2]. The name is in the Maerz and Paul color dictionary [3].

The swatch, #3D9B41, is a clean mid green rather than the yellowish one the word suggests, and its nearest named color is plain [[green]] [3]. Related names include [[chartreuse]], [[avocado]] and [[emerald-green]] [2][3]. The word *bud* in the name points at young growth, though the dictionary says no more [1].

The dictionary treats the word as plain description, with no history attached [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green in only 2 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [4]. This saturated green is rare in the archive [4]. Compare [[celadon]] and [[malachite]] for calmer greens [4]. Screen values for these swatches are approximate [4]. In LCH terms the swatch measures lightness 57, chroma 60 and hue 140 degrees [3].
